artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f(z) = \prod_{i=1}^n (z - \zeta_i)$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n \ge 2$ with pairwise distinct complex roots $\zeta_1,\dots,\zeta_n$. For an initial vector $(x_1^0,\dots,x_n^0) \in \mathbb{C}^n$ of pairwise distinct approximations, consider the generalized Weierstrass (SOR-type) simultaneous iteration
$$x_i^{k+1} \;=\; x_i^k \;-\; h_k \,\frac{f(x_i^k)}{\prod_{j \ne i}(x_i^k - x_j^k)}, \qquad i = 1,\dots,n, \quad k = 0,1,2,\dots,$$
where $h_k \in (0,1]$ is an acceleration (relaxation) parameter that may depend on $k$ and on the current iterate. Setting $h_k \equiv 1$ recovers the classical Weierstrass (Durand–Kerner) method.

Determine a rule for choosing the sequence $\{h_k\} \subset (0,1]$ that (a) guarantees convergence of $(x_1^k,\dots,x_n^k)$ to a permutation of $(\zeta_1,\dots,\zeta_n)$ under explicit, computationally verifiable conditions on the initial approximations, and (b) is optimal among all such guaranteed-convergent choices (for instance, maximizes the convergence rate or the size of the admissible region of initial approximations).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g., works by Proinov, Cholakov, Petković and collaborators from 2015–2024) provides various semilocal convergence theorems for Weierstrass-type SOR methods with parameter h_k ∈ (0,1] under computationally verifiable initial conditions, but no result is reported that identifies a provably optimal guaranteed-convergent choice of h_k. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: Semilocal convergence results for Weierstrass-type methods with acceleration parameter under computationally verifiable initial conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Provides convergence theorems but does not establish an optimal h_k.

status_evidence.title: A note on the convergence of the Weierstrass SOR method for polynomial roots
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes convergence of the SOR-type Weierstrass iteration with relaxation parameter.
status_evidence.claim: Discusses sufficient convergence conditions in terms of h_k without identifying an optimal value.

status_evidence.title: Convergence Analysis of a Modified Weierstrass Method
status_evidence.snippet: Recent convergence analysis for modified Weierstrass-type simultaneous methods.
status_evidence.claim: Continued research indicates the optimal parameter question is not settled.
